request.region_name: Selected map area at 28.75 N, 80.95 W
request.user_question: why did this happen? Is a specific incident or ignition cause documented?

response.explanation_markdown:
The retrieved NASA Earth Observatory report identifies the Iron Horse Fire in northern Brevard County as a regional candidate incident active on February 28, 2011, alongside the Keller and Ferry-7 fires [W1]. According to the report, the Iron Horse Fire burned out of control at approximately 10,000 acres, produced dense smoke that forced closures of Interstate 95 and US Highway 1, threatened homes, and destroyed one home as of March 1 [W1]. Regional reporting does not confirm that the selected map cells fall within that specific fire perimeter, nor does satellite detection data identify individual named fires [K5].

An ignition cause is absent from the retrieved article [W1]. Satellite thermal detections record active combustion but cannot establish how an ignition occurred [K5]. Determining an ignition source requires an official agency investigation report, which remains absent from the retrieved material; consulting local or state wildland fire investigation records for northern Brevard County is a useful next step.

### Satellite observations

The local FIRMS archive contains **22 satellite detections** in the **Selected map area at 28.75 N, 80.95 W** for **2011-02-28** (Aqua, Terra). [5]

citations.relevance_note: Satellite thermal detections alone cannot establish what ignited a fire. Ignition evidence requires a matching investigation or incident report. Wind, high temperature, low humidity and fuel conditions can affect spread but do not establish ignition. A command post location is not necessarily the location of a fire. A regional report is not proof that each selected satellite cell belongs to that incident. A cause absent from retrieved reports is unverified in those reports, not necessarily unknown to authorities.
